title: Molok El-Sook
summary: An Egyptian property-trading party game for up to ten friends, each on their own phone, in Arabic and English.
role: Game design, rules, interface, the 3D board and the multiplayer logic.
description: Molok El-Sook (Kings of the Market) is a property-trading party game for two to ten friends, each playing from their own phone, in Egyptian Arabic or English. The squares are places people know, from Shubra to the North Coast, and the cards speak the way friends do.

The board is new every game. It grows with the number of players, the host picks a map and switches features on or off, and each game draws its own house rules. On a phone the whole game fits one screen with nothing to scroll.

highlights.title: A board that changes
highlights.text: 40, 48 or 56 squares depending on the players, three maps, places drawn from 32 groups, and twist squares placed at random but kept spread out.

highlights.title: A 3D city
highlights.text: The board tilts into a tabletop. Each property grows real 3D buildings as it is upgraded, from a house to a compound, roofed in its owner's colour.

highlights.title: Arabic that agrees with the player
highlights.text: Each player picks a gender, so the cards and the log use the right verb form for everyone at the table.

highlights.title: Fair starts and comebacks
highlights.text: Everyone starts with the same money, the last-place player gets help, and there are bank loans and buyouts so nobody is out of the game early.
